## Question

How does greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agrifood systems for the top 5 producing countries differ and change over the 20 year period from 2001 to 2021?

## Data Source

An API from the World Bank that contains a dataset sourced from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) on GHG emissions from agrifood systems for countries around the world will be used as the source of data to answer the question. More information about this dataset is linked [here](https://data360.worldbank.org/en/indicator/FAO_EMSTOT_6518?view=map).

## Simulation Code & Data Structure

Simulated data will be used to create a data frame of GHG emissions data from agrifood systems for all countries from 2001 to 2021. Wide data format will be used.

```{r}
###Load Packages###

#install.packages("tidyverse")
#install.packages("countrycode") 

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(countrycode) #Used to get the list of countries for the simulated data
```

```{r}
### Create Data Frame###

set.seed(7) # Set seed so that the randomness is reproducible

countries <- codelist$country.name.en # Rename list of countries
years <- 2001:2021 # Label column from year 2001 to 2021

GHGemissionsCountries_SimData <- data.frame( # Create data frame 
  country = rep(countries, each = length(years)),# Create country rows 
  year = rep(years, times = length(countries)), # Create year columns
  GHG_emissions = sample(2:3000000, length(countries) * length(years), replace = TRUE) # Randomly assign GHG emission for each countries cross each year
) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = GHG_emissions) # Produce wide data

head(GHGemissionsCountries_SimData) # Show first 6 rows of data frame

```

## Answer Statement & Simulated Graphs

An answer to the question "How does greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agrifood systems for the top 5 producing countries differ and change over the 20 year period from 2001 to 2021?" can be answered using two graphs:

- A bar chart that compares the average GHG emissions from agrifood systems of the top 5 producing countries for the 20 year period.

- A line graph that demonstrates the changes in GHG emissions from agrifood systems from the top 5 producing countries over the 20 year period from 2001 to 2021.

These graphs will allow for information on which of the 5 countries produced the average highest and lowest GHG emissions from agrifood systems over the 20 year period. They will also provide information on how these countries GHG emissions from agrifood systems changed in regard to each other over the 20 years.

The following steps uses the simulated data to demonstrate how these graphs can be created.

1.  A new column will be added to the data frame to calculate the average GHG emissions from agrifood systems across the 20 year period.
2.  The data will be trimmed to only include the countries with the top 5 highest averages over the 20 year period.
3.  A bar chart of the top 5 countries producing GHG emissions from agrifood systems will be created using the average over the 20 year period to show the comparison between the averages.
4.  A line graph of the top 5 countries producing GHG emissions from agrifood systems between 2001 to 2021 will be created to understand how their production compares to each other across the 20 year period.

### Step 1

```{r}
### Add New Column to Simulated Data Frame###

GHGemissionsCountries_SimData <- GHGemissionsCountries_SimData |> 
  mutate(avg_GHG_emissions = rowMeans(across(`2001`:`2021`))) #Add new column with average GHG emissions over the 20 year period (2001 -2021)

GHGemissionsCountries_SimData <- as_tibble(GHGemissionsCountries_SimData) # Creates table

head(GHGemissionsCountries_SimData) # Displays first 6 rows of the table

```

### Step 2

```{r}
### Create Table of Top 5 Countries Producing the Highest GHG Emissions for Agrifoods systems###

GHGemissionsTop5Countries_SimData <- GHGemissionsCountries_SimData |> 
  slice_max(avg_GHG_emissions, n=5) # Data trimmed to only include the 5 countries with the highest averages

GHGemissionsTop5Countries_SimData # Displays new table

```

### Step 3

```{r}
### Create Bar Chart of the Top 5 Countries Producing the Average Highest GHG Emissions from Agrifoods Systems Over the 20 Year Period###

ggplot(GHGemissionsTop5Countries_SimData, aes(x = avg_GHG_emissions, y = country)) + # Specifies the mapping of the graph
  geom_col() + # Used to create the bar chart
  labs(
    title = stringr::str_wrap(
      "Average GHG Emissions from Agrifood systems for the Top 5 Countries",
      width = 40), # Used to get graph title to fit in the graph space
    x = "Country",
    y = "Average GHG emissions", # Adjusts the labels on the graph
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()

```

### Step 4

```{r}
### Create a Line Graph of the Top 5 Countries Producing GHG emissions from Agrifood systems between 2001 to 2021###

GHG_long <- GHGemissionsTop5Countries_SimData |> # Converts wide data to long data
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `2001`:`2021`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "GHG_emissions"
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))

ggplot(GHG_long, aes(x = year, y = GHG_emissions, colour = country)) + # Create line graph
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "GHG Emissions of the Top 5 Countries",
    x = "Year",
    y = "GHG emissions",
    colour = "Country"
  )

```
